summary: Anthropic researchers study whether automated alignment researchers (AARs) can propose post-training methods and data to mitigate ten well-characterized alignment failures (e.g., deception, sycophancy, jailbreaks) while preserving general capability, comparing results to human researchers and testing generalization to larger models and held-out audits.

practices.reason: Describes using public safety benchmarks and a multi-turn behavioral audit (Petri) to measure alignment failure mitigation, but the method is tied to the lab's own AAR research process rather than a transferable instrument.
practices.quote: The best method remains safer under Petri, a multi-turn behavioral audit.
